cards.title: Read from the centre
items: The reference server is the system under test. Surrounding boxes identify who controls it, which actors exchange protocols with it, and where evidence goes.
The lab harness groups the CLI, scenario runner and supervisor. The server groups the shared runtime and application; these are logical roles, not extra processes.
Owned runtimes can run embedded or as a built process. The supervisor waits for readiness and stops the runtime before closing fixtures; attaching to an existing HTTPS server skips runtime ownership.

The Lab ADE client belongs to the harness and calls Apple directly for API checks, independent readback and explicit restoration. Profile definition, local selection and one-shot assignment use the separate reference-server administration path.

cards.title: Two different environments
items: Simulated runs combine a synthetic device with local Apple-service fixtures. Live runs use real credentials and the appropriate real services.
Contract suites exercise interfaces directly and write their own Go test output. Their results do not flow into lab JSON/JUnit reports.

ABM checks retain current-generation originals and exact exports, verify coverage membership and explicitly correlate authenticated serials. Empty sources remain unexercised; partial synchronization remains blocked.

Designated assignment requires per-device CSV and linkage readback, then restores the original service. Each request keeps separate private recovery evidence; fixture passes do not prove live Apple compatibility.

ADE uses a separate server token: read-only API checks, explicit one-serial profile assignment with an unresolved-outcome fence, and independent native hardware evidence. The fence points to immutable original state and private progress.

Each of macOS, iOS, iPadOS, visionOS and tvOS retains its own result. Stored ADE issuance and fresh native identity, serial, OS/build and supervision observations precede applicable DDM proof; API and fixture success cannot certify hardware.

cards.title: Managed content in the shared runtime
items: The shared server exposes Apps and Books locations, explicit licensing jobs, authenticated callbacks and managed-content operations. API and CLI use dedicated grants; routine principals receive none implicitly. Ordinary reads omit location and callback credentials.

Required capture joins native queue/publication, ownership and sealed state writes. Callback receipts commit before acknowledgment. External Apple requests and APNs delivery run outside those local transactions; unknown outcomes require explicit reconciliation.

Licensing, native dispatch, processing and current installation remain separate observations. Fresh privileged native reads preserve source timestamps. Explicit status-refresh queues owned native queries; neither a command acknowledgment nor APNs acceptance establishes installation.
